theme: The three networking building blocks: URL, URLRequest and URLSession

terms.definition: A Foundation type that represents the address of a web page, a server or a file.
terms.example: Create the URL from a string and check it.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let url = URL(string: "https://x.com/a?id=5")!
print(url.host!, url.path)

terms.definition: A type that describes one request, with its address, method, headers and body.
terms.example: Set the timeout on the URLRequest.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let u = URL(string: "https://x.com/a")!
var r = URLRequest(url: u)
r.timeoutInterval = 10
print(r.url!.path, r.timeoutInterval)

terms.definition: The object that sends requests and receives the replies for your app.
terms.example: Use the shared URLSession for simple calls.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let session = URLSession.shared
let t = session.configuration
print(t.timeoutIntervalForRequest)

video.description:
Learn to explain the objects that send a request: URL, URLRequest & URLSession, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
URL - A Foundation type that represents the address of a web page, a server or a file.
URLRequest - A type that describes one request, with its address, method, headers and body.
URLSession - The object that sends requests and receives the replies for your app.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain URL, URLRequest & URLSession in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
URL, URLRequest, URLSession 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

URL - A Foundation type that represents the address of a web page, a server or a file.
한국어: URL: 웹 페이지, 서버, 파일의 주소를 나타내는 Foundation 타입

URLRequest - A type that describes one request, with its address, method, headers and body.
한국어: URLRequest: 주소, 메서드, 헤더, 바디를 가진 요청 하나를 설명하는 타입

URLSession - The object that sends requests and receives the replies for your app.
한국어: URLSession: 앱을 위해 요청을 보내고 응답을 받는 객체

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about the objects that send a request, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain URL, URLRequest and URLSession in English?

dialogue.title: Loading a profile

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I want to load the profile. Where do I start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: First make a URL. It represents the address of the resource on the server.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. `URL(string:)` returns nil for a bad string, so you can check it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A URLRequest describes one request: the address, the method, headers and body.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do I need a URLRequest for a simple GET?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, you can pass only a URL, but a URLRequest gives you more control.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: URLSession. It sends requests and receives the replies.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, start with the shared URLSession and use a custom one later.

dialogue.code:

let url = URL(string: "https://x.com/a")!
let req = URLRequest(url: url)
let session = URLSession.shared
